### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IAIService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via IAIConversationService (symbol, a top-level interface), IAIService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8323cad97e148fb1955511479adacad19aee10fd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cb636e7e7125ae612bb81e055672783713eb4edd` — the merge of head `c128fd10a116ff96c85f750dc744c70bf7008c6f` into base `8323cad97e148fb1955511479adacad19aee10fd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cb636e7e7125ae612bb81e055672783713eb4edd && git checkout cb636e7e7125ae612bb81e055672783713eb4edd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8323cad97e148fb1955511479adacad19aee10fd c128fd10a116ff96c85f750dc744c70bf7008c6f && git checkout -B drift-repro 8323cad97e148fb1955511479adacad19aee10fd && git merge --no-ff c128fd10a116ff96c85f750dc744c70bf7008c6f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8323cad97e148fb1955511479adacad19aee10fd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8323cad97e148fb1955511479adacad19aee10fd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c128fd10a116ff96c85f750dc744c70bf7008c6f`
Local-runs: none

**Inputs read, and nothing else:** card #23158 (body and all 4 comments: triage 6139367236, claim 6139494839, `os-dev-report` 6140762386, seat ACCEPT 6140802170); PR #23197 body, file list (3 files, +292 / −15) and the net diff against `main`; the head's check-runs, read twice (43 runs each time); code at `origin/main` `8323cad97` and at the head via `git show` / `git grep` only. The seat's ACCEPT was treated as a claim to test, not as evidence. The head is `8aaa06435` merged with `origin/main` `32fa1942e`; `main` has moved 5 commits since, none touching `packages/spec/src/contracts/`, `kernel/execution-context.zod.ts`, `data/data-engine.zod.ts`, `.changeset/pre.json` or the typecheck debt ledger (empty diff-stat over those paths), so the judgments below hold against current `main` too.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface — three interface methods gain an optional trailing parameter. Right.** On `main` (`ai-service.ts` `:447`, `:775`, `:782`) `listPendingActions?(filter?)`, `get(conversationId)` and `list(options?)` carry no context; the head adds `context?: ExecutionContext` as the last parameter of each and one type-only import of `ExecutionContext` from `../kernel/execution-context.zod.js`. No export is added, removed or renamed, and no object, Zod schema, or authorable key moves. The changeset's FROM → TO rows are true to the diff.
2. **Accept set at the type layer — widened, nothing narrowed. Right.** An implementation with fewer parameters remains assignable to each method type (the pin's `shorterGet` / `shorterList` / `shorterListPendingActions`), and a call that omits the argument still compiles (the pin's "omitted" cases are written that way). The only in-repo implementer-shaped code is the mock in `ai-service.test.ts` `:287` (shorter `get` / `list`), whose debt-ledger entry (`TS2739 … getTurnState, update`) is the one it carried before — no new signature arrives, so the ledger stays unmoved. `packages/runtime/src/domains/ai.ts:67` only types a variable and calls none of the three. No implementer of `IAIConversationService` or `IAIService.listPendingActions` exists in this repository; the measured consumer is cloud's `service-ai`, which is still assignable for the same reason.
3. **Type and position — the sibling store contracts' shape. Right.** Counted on `origin/main` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/*.ts` (tests excluded): `sharing-service.ts` 15, `approval-service.ts` 12 and `share-link-service.ts` 3 take a positional `context: ExecutionContext` after the method's own arguments (required); `analytics-service.ts` 3 take the same, optional (`query(query, context?)` `:312`, `generateSql?(…, context?)` `:329`, `queryDataset?` `:351`). `approval-service.ts` `listRequests(filter, context)` `:850` is the same shape as `list(options?, context?)` here. The PR's changeset says "the type and the position", not the optionality — precise, since three of the four siblings make it required and triage asked for optional. The `.js` specifier matches 5 of the 7 sibling imports; the two extensionless ones (`automation-service.ts`, `knowledge-service.ts`) are the minority.
4. **The card asked for an options bag ("the same shape the engine's read verbs take"); triage directed the positional form. The PR follows triage and declares the conflict. Right.** The two forms meet at the engine call: `BaseEngineOptions.context` is `ExecutionContextSchema.partial().optional()` (`data-engine.zod.ts:75`) and `ExecutionContext` is `z.input` of the same schema (`execution-context.zod.ts:518`), so the contract's type is assignable to the engine option with no conversion — pinned by `ForwardsToTheEngineRead`.
5. **TSDoc / changeset sentence — "Under ADR-0096 D5 strict mode an engine read with no principal is refused with 403, so without it an implementation can only read as system." TRUE.** `security-plugin.ts:377` `isPrincipalLessContext` (no `userId`, no `positions`, no `permissions`), `:392` `principalLessDenial` builds `PermissionDeniedError` (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`), thrown at `:8730` inside `resolveOperationPrincipals`, which the engine middleware registered at `:2319` reaches (`:2568`) for every verb after the `isSystem` bypass at `:2365`; `getReadFilter` `:5614` answers the deny filter for the same predicate. A read with no options at all is principal-less by that predicate, so it is refused too. ADR-0096 D5 and its 2026-10-08 note record strict mode ON with no OFF switch, so "under strict mode" is the only mode there is. The two admitted forms are the caller's principal or `isSystem: true` — "can only read as system" is exact.
6. **"passes it unchanged as the `context` of every engine read the method makes." A contract obligation, stated as one. Right.** It is normative text for implementers, not a description of code in this repository (there is none). It is consistent with `IDataEngine.find` / `findOne` `(objectName, query?, options?: BaseEngineOptions)` (`contracts/data-engine.ts:289`, `:306`) and with judgment 4. It binds cloud's `service-ai`, which is not measured here; the pin's header says so.
7. **The `userId` sentence — "`options.userId` stays a filter on the conversation's owner. It is not the caller's identity." TRUE.** `AIConversation.userId` is documented "User who owns the conversation" (`:711`), and `list`'s `userId` filters on it (the existing mock filters `c.userId === options.userId`). Nothing in the contract reads it as a principal.
8. **The access/sharing sentence — "Whether an ordinary member is admitted to their own rows depends on the stored objects' access and sharing, which these contracts do not declare." TRUE.** The contract names no object declaration. `git grep` on `origin/main` for `name: 'ai_conversations'` hits only `plugin-sharing` test fixtures and a `runtime` test; `ai_messages` two test fixtures; `ai_pending_actions` and `ai_agent_memories` zero; the control `name: 'sys_user'` hits 89 files including `platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts`. The liveness ledger (`packages/spec/liveness/agent.json`, `memory` row) places `AgentMemoryStore` and `ai_agent_memories` in cloud.
9. **Pins — what they prove. Right, within their stated limit.** Type level: `Eq` on `Parameters[1]` equals `ExecutionContext | undefined` for each method; arity tuples `1 | 2` and `0 | 1 | 2` prove nothing follows; assignability to the engine option; shorter implementations assigned to the method types. The file is under `src/**/*`, so `tsconfig.test.json` compiles it (`moduleResolution: bundler`, which is why its extensionless relative imports are fine there, as in `data-engine.test.ts` and `objectql-engine.test.ts`), and vitest's `local` project includes `src/**/*.test.ts`. Runtime: a reference implementation over a recording port typed `Pick` of `IDataEngine` shows the supplied context arrive as `options.context` by reference on every read (`get` makes two), `BaseEngineOptionsSchema.safeParse` accepting it, and an omitted context producing a read with no options argument. That half is executable reference for the rule, not a proof about any shipped implementation — the correct limit when no implementer lives here. The dev's ablation reading (0 → 7 pin-file errors per method, type layer) was not re-run; the `Assert` on `Eq` is the shape that reds on reversion, and the verdict here does not rest on it.
10. **Generated artifacts — none owed. Right.** `api-surface/contracts.json` records `IAIConversationService (interface)` by existence only; `api-surface-signatures.json` hashes only the `define*` functions; `export-origins` maps names to files. A method-signature change moves none of them, which matches the diff carrying none.
11. **Scope held to the three named methods. Right.** Inside `IAIService`, `approvePendingAction?(id, actorId)` and `rejectPendingAction?(id, actorId, reason?)` carry an attribution `actorId`, not an execution context; `getTurnState`, `addMessage` and `update` on the conversation service carry none. All are outside the ruling and triage's three; see ③.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening: an optional parameter on three published store-contract methods)` on the PR body's line 2 and in the changeset body. **Right.**

- The diff widens a published type surface (three optional parameters) and narrows nothing, so `yes (widening)` is the true declaration; `widening` is read as non-breaking by `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (signal 4 fires on `narrowing` only), so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed, and none is present. The arm parses: `clause2-line.mjs` reads the first token inside the parenthesis and `(widening:` is admitted (a colon is neither an identifier character nor a pipe).
- Pre mode: `.changeset/pre.json` is `{"mode": "pre", "tag": "next"}` on both `main` and the head, with pending `major` changesets for `@objectstack/spec` already in stock (`11509-…`, the `19939-…` family) and `PROTOCOL_VERSION` `18.0.0` one ahead of the package's `17.7.0` — the lockstep shape `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` admits only in pre mode. Pre mode stands down the launch-window guard on `major`; it does not change the LEVEL axis, which requires a `Clause-②: yes` PR to grade at least one moved published package `minor` or above. `minor` satisfies it, and in the fixed group under a pending major the bump is absorbed into the next `-next` prerelease, so `minor` is the right level and the lowest true one. The `Check Changeset` run on the head concluded success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag (`deviations`, `out_of_scope_findings`; `open_questions` is empty) and the brief's questions, answered or escalated:

- **Deviation 1 — shape (options bag vs positional).** Answered: triage's direction is the binding one and the PR says so rather than resolving it silently; judgment 4 shows the two forms meet at the engine call. No action.
- **Deviation 2 — merged `origin/main` `32fa1942e` before verification.** Answered: the merge is in the head, disjoint from the contract; `main` has moved 5 commits since, none touching the PR's inputs (header above). The queue rebuilds against current `main`.
- **Deviation 3 — the verify lock held 1135 s.** Recorded as fact; no bearing on the contract.
- **Deviation 4 — attribution trailers.** Answered: commit `8aaa06435` carries `Claude-Session:` and the model-free `Co-authored-by` pair AGENTS.md prescribes, and the PR body the session-URL footer. Consistent with the rule that governs this repository.
- **Deviation 5 — file surface held.** Confirmed from the file list: the contract, one pin file beside it, one changeset; no generated artifact, no debt-ledger edit, no `access` or sharing change, no implementation outside spec, no governed surface.
- **Out-of-scope 1 — `getTurnState`, `addMessage`, `update` carry no caller context.** Answered, with a condition: the ruling and triage name exactly three methods, so leaving these three out is right for this PR. The card body's census counts 9 refused reads in cloud's conversation store, which is more than `get` and `list` can account for, so the cloud card that switches the 18 reads back is the right carrier and must say which methods its reads go through; if any goes through one of these three, a follow-up spec card is owed then, with that reading as its evidence. Not a FAIL condition here.
- **Out-of-scope 2 and the brief's H2 question — owner-reads-own-rows NOT MEASURED; card asks 2 and 3 not delivered.** Disposition right: the four objects are declared in cloud (judgment 8), so the measurement cannot run in this repository, and triage ("⛔ no sharing widened as a rider"; the sharing card is filed only on a measurement) forbids filing on an unmeasured premise. The pin's header states the limit. Escalated to the owning seat's landing record: because the PR closes the card with `Fixes #23158` while asks 2 and 3 remain open, the landing record on #23158 must name the cloud card as their carrier so the obligation survives the closure.
- **Check-runs on the head, as read (second read).** Success: `Lint & Repo Gates`, every `Lint ·` sub-job, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` (both runs; one was in progress at the first read), `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, the three claim/closing-target guards, `Auto Label`, `filter`. In progress: `Test Core` 1–6 of 6, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. Skipped: `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, the sharded dogfood matrix entry, one `Auto Label` and one `Check PR Size` duplicate. No run has failed. The required `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` contexts had not concluded at read, so the PR is not yet green for the queue; this verdict is on the diff, and the landing still waits for every check green.
- **PR shape for the landing.** Draft, same-repo head, 307 changed lines, label `needs:contract-review` present, no governed path in the file list. Nothing here reserves the landing beyond this record and green checks.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23158-ai-store-caller-context`
Reviewed-by: `session_012uFegdfR6K6uqvLzt7XsdZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**
